newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria opposed to Germany funding EU jobs plan.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria opposed to Germany funding EU jobs plan.

text.p: A senior Bavarian politician said on Wednesday the large southern German state was oopposed to any European employment initiative for which Germany would have to pick up much of the bill.

"Jobs programmes only work when they are backed by lots of money and it would be mainly Germany that would be called on to finance these programmes," Bavarian state minister Kurt Faltlhauser said in speech in Munich.

Faltlhauser, a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU) party that is a core part of the German coalition government, was outlining the European policies of the Bavarian state government ahead of next week's EU summit in Amsterdam.

Faltlhauser said it would further be unacceptable if an employment chapter in the EU treaty was agreed there which would allow job creation programmes to be launched with the backing of only a qualified majority of member states.
"I can only hope that Chancellor Helmut Kohl succeeds in Amsterdam pulling the rudder back round again when it comes to the formulation of the employment chapter," Faltlhauser said.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel earlier said the German federal government was not opposed to an employment chapter in principle, on condition it would not incur extra spending for "unfinanceable" job creation schemes. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
